issues.title: Inline --sql tip is printed to stdout and corrupts the default JSON output

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
cd D:/workspace/Browser4/Browser4-4.14
./b4w.ps1 -s books-eval htmlsnapshot query --sql "SELECT DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, 'h1') AS t FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, ':root')" > out.json 2> err.txt
python -c "import json; json.load(open('out.json'))"

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: stdout carries exactly the JSON envelope (the default --format json is documented as the clean machine-readable mode), the tip is suppressed or goes to stderr, and stderr/exit code carry any diagnostics.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: stdout contains the JSON envelope + a blank line + 3 tip lines ('💡 Tip: Use --sql @file.sql to avoid shell quoting issues...'); stderr is empty; exit code is 0. json.loads on the whole stdout fails with 'Extra data: line 3 column 1 (char 474)'. Only the inline --sql form triggers it (not @file, --sql-stdin or --sql-base64), but that is the form shown in the command's own examples. SKILL.md also states tips are suppressed by default and appear on stderr, which this contradicts.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: In cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs, handle_html_snapshot_query() computes `let structured_stdout = output_file.is_none() && format != "json";` and then `emit_tip` uses `cli_println!` (stdout) when structured_stdout is false, `eprintln!` when true. Because the DEFAULT format is json, the condition evaluates the default case as 'human output' and writes the tip onto the same stream as the payload; the comment above it states the opposite intent (keep machine-readable output clean). The tip is also emitted whenever SQL was inline (is_inline_sql), with no --show-tip gating.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_html_snapshot_query() (tip emission at ~lines 11016-11039)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Treat the default JSON envelope as structured stdout: use `output_file.is_none()` (or `format != "table" && format != "csv"`) so the tip goes to stderr for --format json too.
- Alternatively route every tip/hint to stderr unconditionally, and reserve stdout for the payload the user asked for.
- Gate this hint behind --show-tip (as SKILL.md describes) or emit it at most once per session.
- Add a regression test that pipes `htmlsnapshot query --sql <inline>` stdout into a JSON parser and asserts it parses.

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect's truncation hint names a selector that silently returns empty strings

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s books-eval htmlsnapshot inspect  # prints: DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, 'a', 'title') → "A Light in the Attic"
./b4w.ps1 -s books-eval htmlsnapshot query --sql "SELECT DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, 'a', 'title') AS suggested, DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, 'h3 a', 'title') AS actual FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, 'article.product_pod', 1, 3)"
./b4w.ps1 -s books-eval htmlsnapshot get all attr "a" title --limit 8

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The SQL snippet printed next to the sample value returns that value for each item (here the full book titles from the title attribute), or the tool warns that the ref is not directly usable as a container-scoped selector.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The query returns suggested="" for all rows while the true selector 'h3 a' returns "A Light in the Attic"/"Tipping the Velvet"/…; the suggested `get all attr "a" title` returns ["","","","","","","",""]. No error is raised, so a first-time user (or an agent following the tool's own advice) gets a silently empty title column.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The backend builds the hint's childSelector with buildElementRef(target), which yields a standalone tag/class ref of the element that carries the fuller text ('a'), not a selector path relative to the repeating container ('h3 a'). Inside each article.product_pod the first matching <a> is the image link, which has no title attribute, so DOM_FIRST_ATTR / get all resolve to a different element and return "". The CLI then renders that ref verbatim as a SQL selector.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/mcp/controller/MCPToolController.kt:inspectDocument() (truncation-hint block ~lines 2547-2580, selector from buildElementRef() at ~line 2977); rendered by cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_html_snapshot_inspect() (~line 12111 for the SQL snippet, ~line 12333 for the `get all attr` line)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Build the hint selector relative to the inspected container (e.g. 'h3 a' via the same selector-derivation used for 'Suggested selectors'), not from a standalone element ref.
- Validate the emitted selector before printing it: re-run it scoped to the sample and drop the hint if the attribute comes back empty.
- When only an element ref is known, say so explicitly ('the element matching ref <x> carries title=…') instead of emitting it as a DOM_FIRST_ATTR CSS argument.
- Add a books.toscrape.com-shaped fixture test asserting the suggested SQL returns the full title for every row.

issues.title: Inspect offers no directly usable X-SQL selector for the page's key field (titles)

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s books-eval htmlsnapshot inspect   # then read the 'Suggested selectors' block and try the printed title-related suggestions

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: For a repeated listing whose title is clipped in the markup, inspect should name a plain, SQL-ready selector path for the title (e.g. h3 a).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The title is covered only by `h3:expr(a>0)` (printed with the warning that :expr() works in the FROM clause/get but NOT inside DOM_* X-SQL args, i.e. unusable in the SELECT list) and `h3` (listed under 'Structural (bare tags, low specificity) ... use only as a fallback'). The working selector `h3 a` never appears; the only title-oriented snippet is the broken truncation hint of the previous issue. The user must hand-derive `h3 a`.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The selector suggester emits bare tag names and PowerCSS :expr variants for nested elements but no plain descendant combinations, and the truncation hint (the intended bridge from clipped text to the title attribute) carries an unusable standalone ref.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_html_snapshot_inspect() (selector suggestion rendering); browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/mcp/controller/MCPToolController.kt:inspectDocument() (selector ranking)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Rank and emit plain descendant selectors ('h3 a', 'h3 > a') when a nested element is the unique carrier of a field, not only bare tags and :expr() forms.
- When a suggested selector would be unusable in the target context (e.g. :expr inside DOM_* args), either suppress it from the X-SQL-oriented list or offer the plain equivalent next to it.
- Print one ready-to-run X-SQL snippet for the most salient field of the repeated row (title/price/link), which is what listing pages are inspected for.

issues.title: tab-list reports the only tab as inactive and shows the pre-redirect URL

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s books-eval tab-list --json
./b4w.ps1 -s books-eval page-info

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: With exactly one tab, that tab reports active:true; the URL matches the page actually shown (https after the http->https redirect).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: tab-list --json: {"tabs":[{"index":0,...,"url":"http://books.toscrape.com/","title":"All products | Books to Scrape - Sandbox","active":false}],"count":1} while page-info reports https://books.toscrape.com/ for the same tab. In the earlier two-tab state BOTH entries reported active:false, so no tab was ever marked active.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Not investigated in depth. Likely the backend tab enumeration does not mark the session's current target as active (field left false), and tab-list reports the last navigated URL rather than the landed URL after redirects; both need checking in the tab-listing path.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Mark the session's current tab active in tab-list output, and assert the invariant 'exactly one active tab'.
- Report the landed URL (post-redirect) in tab-list, or label the field as the navigated URL if the pre-redirect form is intentional.
- Cover it with a test that opens a redirecting URL and compares tab-list vs page-info.

issues.title: Duplicate tab appeared once and was not reproducible

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Session sequence: open --headless -> htmlsnapshot inspect (auto) -> inspect "article.product_pod" -> query (inline) -> query (@file) -> query (--sql-stdin) -> query (--sql-base64) -> query --result-only -> get all attr "a" title -> get all attr "h3 a" title -> page-info. Then: ./b4w.ps1 -s books-eval page-info  # printed 'Page 0' and 'Page 1'; ./b4w.ps1 -s books-eval tab-list --json  # count 2, both on https://books.toscrape.com/

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Read-only extraction commands leave the session with the single tab that was opened; page-info lists one page.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Two identical tabs existed in the session at the end of that sequence (only open, a navigation, was ever supposed to create a tab). Replaying every command of the sequence on a fresh session (close, open, inspect, query, query --sql-base64, query --sql-stdin, get all, page-info) kept the tab count at 1 after each step, so the trigger is unknown.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Unknown. Candidates: the session/browser launch restoring a previous target, or a command on the page-load path opening a helper target that is never closed. Needs instrumented logging of Target.createTarget callers per command.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Log which component opens each CDP target (and why) at debug level so a stray tab can be attributed.
- Add an invariant check/test: after each read-only htmlsnapshot command, the session's tab count must be unchanged.
- Document explicitly if any read path (e.g. -readonly loads) may open a target, so users are not surprised by extra entries in tab-list.

issues.title: --sql-base64 help example cannot run in PowerShell

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 help htmlsnapshot query   # example: browser4-cli htmlsnapshot query --sql-base64 "$(base64 -w0 query.sql)"  — paste it into PowerShell

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A copy-pasteable example for the CLI's primary platform shell (b4w.ps1 targets Windows/PowerShell), or a per-shell pair.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The example is POSIX-only ($(...) command substitution and base64 -w0 do not exist in PowerShell); the Windows equivalent ([Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes(...))) is documented only for eval --base64 in references/eval.md.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The example block for htmlsnapshot query in cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs (~line 1211) was written from a bash perspective only.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs (htmlsnapshot query examples block, ~line 1211)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add the PowerShell form next to the POSIX one, e.g. --sql-base64 ([Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('query.sql'))).
- Label the existing line as 'bash / macOS' and mirror the eval.md wording for Windows.
- Verify examples per platform in CI (a smoke test that runs each documented example under both shells).
